Forms FOREWORD 

The solicitor will do well to draw all of his forms rather than to rely upon the Clerk to do so, with the exception of the citation which by statute the Clerk must issue and which in practice he always prepares. To delegate to the Clerk the drawing of forms, other than citation, means delay and lack of opportunity to correct any errors which may be made.

In suits for divorce, the pleadings are entitled and endorsed in the names of the respective parties, each designated by the surname of the husband, as Ella Smith v. John Smith.

In drafting the petition for divorce, the first paragraph should set forth the date and place of the marriage. In the forms hereinafter suggested, these allegations are set forth in language applicable alike to ceremonial and so-called "common law" marriages. 

The pleader may, but need not, set forth the name of the person who performed the ceremony, and his office, as in the old forms, nor is it necessary to set forth the performance or non-performance of a marriage ceremony. 

The second paragraph should set forth the cause of action, and the third paragraph the domiciliary jurisdictional requirements within sections 2:50-10 and 2:50-11 of the Revision. Care should be taken to select that form of paragraph 3 which sets forth the necessary jurisdictional allegations of residence under the circumstances of the particular case. To this end, before drafting the petition it should be ascertained whether or not personal service of process can be effected in New Jersey, and whether or not at the time the cause of action arose either of the parties was domiciled here. In extreme cruelty and adultery cases the cause of action arises upon the commission of the offense; in desertion cases it arises upon the expiration of two years from the commencement of the desertion, whether the desertion is simple or constructive. 

If personal service of process upon the defendant can be effected in this state, then, if either of the parties was a bona fide resident of this state at the time the cause of action arose, and has continued so to be for a period of at least two years and down to the date of the filing of the petition, a suit for absolute divorce may be brought upon any one or more of the three grounds. In suits 669

670 

FORMS FOREWORD 

for absolute divorce for adultery, and in suits for limited divorce on any ground, the period of residence need not be longer than the period between the date of the offense and the date of filing the petition, even though such period be less than two years. 

If personal service of process can be made within this state but neither party was a bona fide resident of New Jersey at the time the cause of action arose, then, if either party becomes a bona fide resident of this state after the cause of action has arisen, and continues so to be for a period of at least two years and down to the date of filing the petition, a suit for divorce, either absolute or from bed and board, may be brought upon any of the three grounds, provided that the cause of action alleged was recognized in the jurisdiction in which such party resided at the time the cause of action arose as ground for the same relief asked for in the action in this state. 

If personal service of process cannot be made in this jurisdiction, then, if the petitioner was a bona fide resident of New Jersey at the time the cause of action arose, and has continued so to be for a period of at least two years and down to the date of filing the petition, a suit for absolute divorce may be brought upon any of the three grounds. In suits for absolute divorce for adultery, and for limited divorce on any ground, such term of residence may be less than two years.

If personal service of process cannot be made within the jurisdiction, and the petitioner was not a bona fide resident of New Jersey at the time the cause of action arose, then, if the petitioner has become such resident since the cause of action arose, and for at least two years next preceding the commencement of the action has continued so to be, a suit for divorce, absolute or from bed and board, will lie upon any of the three grounds, provided that the cause of action alleged was recognized in the jurisdiction in which the petitioner resided when such cause of action arose as a ground for the same relief asked for in the action in this state.

Divorce From Bed and Board (a Mensa Et Thoro) 

A divorce from bed and board may be decreed upon any of the three grounds upon which divorces from the bond of matrimony may be predicated. Essentially there is no difference in the forms of petition used, save in the prayer, and in extreme cruelty cases the six months' limitation applicable to divorces from the bond of matrimony does not apply.

If it is desired to secure a decree of divorce from bed and board rather than a dissolution of the marriage, the petition suitable as to the ground and as to the domiciliary requirements may be selected from those heretofore exhibited, and the prayer changed, by omitting the words, "Petitioner prays that the marriage between the petitioner and defendant may be dissolved for the cause aforesaid, etc.," and substituting the words, "Petitioner prays that

F 753 

BED AND BOARD 

she may be divorced from the bed and board of said defendant for the cause aforesaid, etc."

The domiciliary requirements in bed and board cases are the same as those in suits for divorce from the bond of matrimony on the ground of adultery and differ from the requirements in desertion and cruelty cases for divorce, as will be seen by reference to Foreword immediately preceding Form 1 and supra §§168, 198, 239. The following form of petition for divorce from bed and board for extreme cruelty may also be used as a guide in other cases.

 C.

NULLITY OF MARRIAGE 

In nullity suits, whether brought on grounds rendering the marriage void or only voidable, the papers should be entitled so that the woman is referred to by her name as it was before the void or voidable marriage, with the addition of the words, "falsely called" or "otherwise," followed by the surname of the male party to the defective marriage. For example: John Jones, petitioner, v. Mary 

Smith, falsely called Mary Jones, defendant. Or, Mary Smith, otherwise Mary Jones, petitioner, v. John Jones, defendant.¹

Petitioner and defendant have been for many years close neighbors and childhood friends, being of about the same age, having attended the same classes in school and being in the same social circle of friends. On the .. day of ......, 19.., petitioner and defendant were driving by automobile with their respective parents and other friends to visit relatives of your petitioner in the City of Baltimore, State of Maryland. A stop was made for luncheon at Elkton, Maryland, and while the other members of the party were still at lunch petitioner and defendant took a walk together along some of the streets. In front of many houses there appeared signs advertising that marriages were performed in said houses. Defendant laughingly proposed that he and petition go into one of these houses and pretend to be married, as a joke on their friends and the members of their party. Petitioner, in a spirit of fun, and not realizing or intending that a binding marriage would be performed, consented and accompanied defendant into one of said houses. A marriage ceremony was performed within a few minutes and petitioner and defendant thereupon rejoined the other members of the party who had finished their lunch and were awaiting petitioner and defendant with some impatience. Defendant laughingly announced that he and petitioner had been married and their delay was occasioned thereby. 

None of the party regarded defendant's statement seriously, but merely as a joke. The party proceeded to Baltimore. Petitioner, commencing that evening to feel uneasy regarding the pretended ceremony of marriage, spoke again of it to her parents. At first they still did not take it seriously, but gradually, as petitioner related the circumstances, and the details of the ceremony, they realized that a ceremony of marriage had actually been performed, as aforesaid, and that the matter was serious. Thereupon they sent for the defendant, who was spending the night in a hotel nearby. He came at once and admitted that the ceremony had been a joke and that he had had no intention of actually marrying petitioner. Said pretended marriage has been in no wise consummated, ratified or confirmed.

Inspection for Impotence 

NOTE 1: The following forms (Forms 146-150) of order for commission to inspect, etc., are for use in all contested cases. Under the ecclesiastical practice it was customary to appoint one physician and one surgeon, and that may still be done. In case the defendant is the husband, the words in the order and commission, "whether she is a virgin," are omitted, and in place thereof, "whether he is capable of performing the act of generation," is substituted therefor. 

NOTE 2: These forms may readily be adapted to cases where inspection is sought previous to hearing. In uncontested cases, instead of the method of identification employed in the following forms, the order for commission should provide that the inspectors state in their return how the defendant was identified, and that the return contain a description of the defendant so that the court may be certain of his or her identity.

PROCESS IN DIVORCE AND NULLITY SUITS 

No attempt has been made to include any but the forms commonly used under this heading. Many others might have been included, but have been omitted as being more confusing than helpful. In special cases, by following the suggestions contained in Chapter 17 supra, the practitioner should have no difficulty in drafting suitable variants of the common forms herein set forth.

her mother and had no present intention of making any change of her residence or occupation. 

 (Signature and Title of Officer) (Add Typed Signature) 

The grounds of affiant's knowledge must be stated with sufficient particularity to show clearly that affiant has actual, personal knowledge of the present residence of defendant. Otherwise, the proof cannot be accepted in lieu of the prescribed inquiry under Rule 276, regardless of the strength of the factual basis for affiant's belief as to defendant's residence. Affiant's knowledge must be personal, actual and first-hand, not hearsay.

Rule 276 does not require that the description shall give more than the age, residence and occupation of the defendant. The note following Form 168 should be consulted.

If the application for order dispensing with special substituted service is made at the same time as for the order for publication, draft of order dispensing (Form 176) should be submitted. The order for publication will then be entered in the usual form (Form 173) prescribing publication and substituted service, and the order dispensing will be entered immediately thereafter. If petitioner's affidavits (Forms 168, 169) are executed but a few days before the application is made for the order dispensing, they will be accepted. But if they are executed more than a few days previously, supplemental affidavits will be required reporting upon the facts to date (Forms 170, 171). It should be borne in mind that established practice calls for the order for publication in such cases to prescribe substituted service, and the entry of a separate order dispensing therewith if the proofs of inquiry warrant. The latter order must be entered within twenty days after the date of the order for publication.

Upon filing a petition for divorce, or nullity of marriage, the Clerk issues the citation. The return day has been abolished, and the answer must now be filed within twenty days after service.

Form 175 is to be used where the application for special substituted service is made subsequent to entry of order for publication. If the application is made at the same time as the application for the order for publication, the combining form (Form 174 or 174A) should be used, rather than the two separate orders (as in Forms 173 and 175). This form (Form 175) may be adapted to fit a case where a special substituted service was effected within time but without an order first obtained. In such case the order may be entered nunc pro tunc as of time, adopting the service made as that which would have been directed had. application been made within time.

by defendant, which is now in my possession ready to be produced, which letter reads as follows: No. Street, San Francisco, Cal., 19... 

My dear....:

I have concluded that we ought not to continue our matrimonial relations in the future. I think you know, and I assure you that I had an affectionate and true regard for you, and appreciate your many good qualities and kindnesses.

The fact is, however, that we have outgrown each other. 

Your tastes and mine are utterly dissimilar, and the things which each of us desire most earnestly are not within the other's power or interest to give.

I want a home such as I have here in California, and such as I had in my early years, where I can have my friends, my garden, and the feeling of peace and rest that comes through understanding and sympathetic companionship. This you cannot give me.

I realize that your attitude toward me must be much the same as mine toward you. You cannot really desire that our friendship as husband and wife continue under these circumstances.

I have left you more than well provided for financially, and 

I now ask you to let me have my freedom. I am convinced that it is as much for your good as for mine. In any case, do you not think that all of the things that I have done for you are sufficient justification for your doing one thing for me. 

You may dread what people may say, but that consideration should not weigh heavily with you, in view of the consciousness you will have of doing a thing that you know is good and generous. 

As I see it, neither of us is to blame. Certainly you have done no wrong; I am simply trying to get you to make right a grievous mistake, which you and I both made when we married each other twenty years ago.

It will be very much more to your credit and social standing with your friends if you apply for the divorce and have everything arranged quietly. 

Most sincerely yours,

If the decree for divorce was based upon publication and substituted service of process, that fact should be stated in the petition; in such case, if the defendant can be personally served in 

New Jersey with the order to show cause [Form 211], the court will have jurisdiction in personam for the purpose of ordering alimony and maintenance based upon the above petition. In case the defendant was not served with process in the main suit and cannot be served with a copy of the order to show cause, the petitioner will not be entitled to relief in personam and can secure relief only in rem, if property of the defendant can be found located in the State of New Jersey. The wife's proceeding in that case is not by petition as above, but by sequestration, as in 

Maloney v. Maloney, 12 N. J. Misc. 397, 174 Atl. 28 (1934), Forms 411, 412.

C. Form 230 

Maintenance-Answer Denying Charges of Extreme Cruelty, 

Abandonment and Non-support 

(Title of Cause)

Form 235 may be adapted for use where there has been a ceremonial marriage which the defendant claims is void. In such case the facts should be clearly stated, so that issue may be joined thereon. If the defendant claims that the marriage was voidable rather than void, however, he must attack it directly, and may do so by means of a counterclaim in the separate maintenance suit.

 C.

A final decree in a maintenance suit may be entered without proofs upon the consent of the defendant, in which case the consent should be recited in the decree and should appear at the foot thereof in writing, over the signature of the defendant rather than that of his solicitor, or in addition thereto. 

The final decree may contain provision for a bond or other security for the payment of the sums decreed, and may contain provision for the custody, education, support and visitation of the children. (See the clauses in decrees nisi, Forms 75-80.) It is not necessary to provide at the foot of the decree that either party be at liberty to apply for a variance or modification, because the statute gives this right.

If upon the final decree there are arrears under an ad interim maintenance order, a provision should be inserted in the final decree for the payment of such arrearages, as otherwise they are deemed to have been waived or paid. (See Form 79.)

The court has jurisdiction to provide that alimony payments commence at any day prior to final decree, but not as of a date prior to the filing of the bill. Form 237 may be modified accordingly in such cases.

In a case where the husband had conveyed real estate without consideration for the purpose of defeating his wife's dower, as well as her right to maintenance, the final decree may be drafted as in 

Form 238.

It is important that the recital of this order show the ground upon which the bill was dismissed, that is, what jurisdictional fact the proofs failed to establish, or, if the suit was dismissed because of the establishment by the defendant of some special defense, such as recrimination, that fact should be recited. The importance of accuracy in the recitals lies in the evidential value of the decree in a subsequent matrimonial suit between the parties.

FOURTH: If any doubt should arise as to the true meaning or purpose of this trust agreement, the Donor declares for the purpose of aiding in the interpretation and construction thereof that it is the general intent of this trust agreement to set aside the principal hereinabove provided, for the purpose of securing the Beneficiary an annual net income of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000), and no more, from the earnings of the said principal to be paid to the Beneficiary throughout the period of her natural life and irrespective of any other income which she may derive from any source whatever and thereafter to pay the same as herein provided. 

FIFTH: During the continuance of the trust agreement hereby created the Trustee shall not be liable in any way for the character or safety of the securities above mentioned, or of any substitution thereof, so far as their market value is concerned and so long as the said trustee shall comply with the provisions of this agreement. 

SIXTH: The Donor hereby reserves to himself during the continuance of the trust and throughout the period of his lifetime, the right to require the said Trustee, pursuant to notice in writing by him given, to vary, transfer or transpose any or all of the securities above enumerated either by sale and purchase or by exchange into or for other stocks, bonds, shares or securities, the income of which shall in the aggregate amount to the sum of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000) annually; and further and in the same manner to continue to vary, transfer or transpose any or all of said securities during and throughout the period aforesaid, always provided, however, that such variation, transfer or transposal of any or all of such securities shall be made with the approval and consent of the Trustee, endorsed in writing at the time upon its copy of the trust agreement, it being understood and agreed that the said Trustee in exercising its discretion in the giving or granting of its consent and approval for the variation, transfer or substitution of one security for another shall be actuated in good faith for the purpose of maintaining the principal of the trust funds in such form and of such character as to produce a net income to the Beneficiary of

Form 254 

Answer and Counterclaim in Phillips v. Phillips 5 

The defendant, 

residing at.... in the County of and State of New Jersey, says: 

1. Paragraphs 1 to 6 inclusive of the complaint are admitted. 

2. Paragraph 7 of the complaint is denied.

First Defense DEFENSES TO THE COMPLAINT 

The agreement, upon which specific performance and the decree of this court for the payment of money is sought, is void in fact because it was and is against the public policy of this state in that said agreement was the result of collusion between the parties to said agreement; was entered into between the parties thereto in order to facilitate the procurement by the complainant of a decree for divorce against the defendant; was entered into in order to enable the complainant to procure a divorce and one of the considerations for said contract was the agreement by defendant not to defend said suit for divorce.

By reason thereof, complainant is not now entitled to enforce said agreement.

Second Defense 

The agreement, upon which specific performance and the decree of this court for the payment of money is sought, is, insofar as the provisions thereof relate to the payment of $10,000 per year during the life of the complainant, an agreement respecting alimony, support and maintenance of the complainant, made during the time when divorce proceedings were pending between them in the State of New Jersey; said agreement was entered into without the consent or approval of this court; the terms and conditions thereof have not been approved by this court; the terms and conditions thereof, insofar as they require the payment of $10,000 per year to the complainant during her life, are unfair, inequitable 

5. Phillips v. Phillips, 118 N. J. Eq. 189, 178 Atl. 265 revd. 119 N. J. Eq. 

462, 183 Atl. 220 and affd. 119 N. J. Eq. 497, 183 Atl. 222; supra § 487.

F 951 

SUPPORT AGREEMENTS 

and unjust insofar as defendant is concerned. Said terms and conditions were and are also unsuitable and improper for the support of the complainant, were and are grossly in excess of her just needs and demands, and were and are far beyond the power and ability of the defendant to comply therewith. Defendant was and is unable to comply therewith and says that by reason thereof it is inequitable that said agreement should be enforced or that defendant be decreed to comply therewith.

Third Defense 

The complaint does not state a cause of action cognizable in equity in that the court is without jurisdiction to decree specific performance of the agreement set forth in the complaint. 

Defendant prays that the bill be dismissed, with costs.

COUNTERCLAIM 

By way of counterclaim exhibited by the defendant against the complainant, the defendant says that: 

1. He repeats the allegations of the second defense. 

2. He prays that this court examine into, revise and modify the agreement referred to in the complaint, so that that part thereof which provides for the payment of the sum of $10,000 per year may be revised and modified so as to provide for such payments as may be equitable, just and fair to both of the parties thereto. (Solicitor for and of 

The complainant moved to strike the answer and counterclaim and the court struck out the counterclaim and all of the answer except the First Defense of collusion, 118 N. J. Eq. 189, 178 Atl. 

265. On appeal, the court's refusal to strike out the defense of collusion was affirmed, 119 N. J. Eq. 497, 183 Atl. 222, but the court's order striking out the Third Defense of lack of jurisdiction was reversed, 119 N. J. Eq. 462, 183 Atl. 222.

Because of the presently unsettled state of the law on the subject of the enforcement of contracts for support (see supra § 487), the pleadings are given for what they may be worth.

FIRST SEPARATE DEFENSE 

1. On or about November 21, 1932, complainant and her agents and representatives, in order to induce defendant to enter into and execute a written separation agreement between them, bearing date of November 21, 1932, did then and there state and represent to him that one .... ... did not pay any visits to, call upon or speak to complainant since the date the said ..... was expelled from the home of complainant and defendant. 

2. Relying upon the truth of the statements and representations made to him as aforesaid, and by reason thereof, defendant did then and there enter into and execute the aforesaid separation agreement. 

3. Subsequently defendant discovered and learned that the statements and representations made to him as aforesaid, all of which he believed to be true at the time, were in fact false and

known so to be to the said complainant at the time of their making, because the said ... did, on divers times and occasions from the time of his expulsion from the home of complainant and defendant up to the time of the making of the said statements and representations by complainant and her agents as aforesaid, pay visits, call upon and speak to complainant. 

4. By reason of the foregoing false representations and fraudulent conduct on the part of the complainant and her agents and representatives in procuring the said separation agreement from defendant, said agreement is of no force or effect. 

SECOND SEPARATE DEFENSE 

1. In addition to the statements and representations made by complainant, her agents and representatives to defendant as particularly set forth in the First Separate Defense herein above, and in order to induce defendant to execute the said separation agreement, complainant, her agents and representatives, did also then and there state and represent to defendant that complainant would not receive, accept or entertain any calls, visits or conversations of the said at any time thereafter. ... 

2. Relying upon the truth of all of the foregoing statements and representations, and by reason thereof, defendant entered into and executed the aforementioned separation agreement. 

3. Defendant subsequently learned and ascertained that at the time of the making of the statements and representations aforementioned, complainant did not intend to fulfill or carry them out, but made same solely for the purpose of deceiving defendant into entering into and executing the aforesaid separation agreement and leaving their home pursuant to its terms. 

4. Contrary to the statements and representations made to defendant as aforesaid, complainant thereafter did, on divers times and occasions, receive visits from and entertain and speak to the said .... at her home and elsewhere. 

5. By reason of the deceit and fraud perpetrated by complainant upon defendant in connection with procuring the aforementioned separation agreement, the said separation agreement was and is null and void.

Form 271

Non-Prosecution-Order for Leave to Proceed and to 

Answer-Uncontested Cause (Rule 286) 

The following order is to be entered when the delay occurred after process was served or jurisdiction was acquired over defendant under an order for publication. 

It appearing that the above stated cause has been suffered to lie without substantial prosecution for upwards of one year, and petitioner now applying for leave to proceed herein; and it further appearing by affidavit that the relations of the parties to each other have not changed pending this suit, nor has the cause of action alleged in the petition been condoned by the petitioner, and that the delay was occasioned by (here state the facts), and that the suit is not sought to be proceeded with by any collusion between the petitioner and defendant, but in truth and good faith for the causes set forth in the petition; and the court being of opinion that further opportunity should be afforded to the defendant to answer; 

It is thereupon, on this .. day of ..... 19., ordered that petitioner have leave to proceed with this cause and that defendant do answer the petitioner's petition within.. days after service upon him of a certified copy of the petition and of this order, or in default of such answer, that the Chancellor may make such further order in this cause as shall be agreeable to law and the practice of this court.

F 965 

NON-PROSECUTION 

It should be borne in mind that the service prescribed is upon defendant within or without the state, if practicable. Such service must be made, though service by registered mail upon a nonresident defendant resulting in a personally signed registry return card is accepted. The provisions of Rule 191 do not strictly apply so far as Rule 286 provides otherwise as to service. 

Impracticability of service warrants entry of order dispensing with service of order to answer. The above form may be varied in such case to contain an additional appropriate recital that defendant's whereabouts cannot be ascertained after due inquiry therefor, and the order to answer clause should direct that service of an order to answer pursuant to Rule 286 be dispensed with. In such case, in addition to the affidavit under Rule 286, proofs of a complete inquiry for defendant's whereabouts should be submitted under Rule 276.

Form 296 Clerk

Abstract of Decree and Order Fixing Arrearages to Be Filed 

With Clerk of Supreme Court

In order to secure execution out of the Supreme Court for arrearages of alimony, etc., it is necessary that the abstract to be filed under the statute show that the Court of Chancery has definitely fixed and established the amount of arrearages. For this purpose an order in Chancery must be entered, on notice, fixing such arrearages, before the abstract will be effective. See Rooney v. Rooney, 102 N. J. Law 551, 133 Atl. 752 (1926).

Form 300 

Exceptions to Master's Report 

The defendant, this cause by .. 

(Title of Cause) 

hereby excepts to the report filed in one of the Special Masters of this court, 19. ., for the following reasons: 

bearing date the .. day of 

1. That the Master has found that the estrangement between the petitioner and his two children was due to the adverse influence which the mother has exercised over the children, whereas the evidence discloses that such estrangement was not in any way due to the influence of the mother but was entirely due to the conduct of the father in having failed to communicate with his children, to see or speak with his children ever since the custody of these children was awarded to the mother by the decree of this court. 

2. That the Master found that the father was ready, willing and able to maintain and provide for the said children in his own home although the evidence discloses that the father of these children never made any attempt to see the children, speak to the children or write to the children ever since the custody of said children had been awarded to the mother by the decree of this court, and although by the terms of said decree right of access had been

F 987 

EXCEPTIONS 

awarded the petitioner, which right was never exercised or attempted to be exercised by him. 

3. That the Master found that it would be grossly unconscionable to require the petitioner to accede to the demands of the defendant that he provide an additional room in the home of the defendant and her present husband at which the children may live during their summer vacation and on their visits home from school, because the father had offered to have the children live with him, whereas the Master should have found that the father's offer was not bona fide in view of his conduct with respect to these children and to have found that these children were entitled to be furnished with a room in the home of their mother for the periods of time at which they visited the mother. 

4. That the Master found that the attitude of the father toward his children is understandable under the circumstances; that he sincerely seeks the love and affection of his children; that to that end the court should stand with him in offering additional inducements to the children so that he may regain the position in their hearts and minds to which he, as their father, is entitled, although the evidence discloses that the conduct of the father toward the children and his attitude ever since the entry of the decree of divorce was anything but commendable and that the children justifiably regarded him as a complete stranger unto themselves, and that under the circumstances the children should not have been penalized by the Master by depriving them of the various necessities that they would otherwise be entitled to. 

5. That the Master erred in finding that the various requirements of the children as to dancing lessons, musical instruction, sport activities and summer camp should be withheld from them because of their refusal to live with their father. 

6. That the Master erred in going beyond the provisions of the order of reference in receiving evidence concerning the custody of these children, and in making determinations based upon the refusal of the children to accept the offer of their father to have them live with him. 

7. That the Master erred in deeming it unnecessary to consider the mode of living of the father and the fact that he has made expenditures during the past year of over $2,000 a month; that the 

Master erred in regarding the expenditures of the father and the mode of living of the father as an academic question. 

8. That the Master erred in failing to give consideration to the expenditures made by the defendant out of her own income and borrowed moneys for the support and maintenance of these children. 1

F 301 

EXCEPTIONS 

9. That the Master erred in finding that the sum of $1600 per annum is the sum which the father, the petitioner, should be required to pay for the support and maintenance of the said 

and 

10. That the Master should have found from the evidence that the father should be required to pay a minimum of $400 a month for the support and maintenance of the aforementioned two children; that the Master erred in failing to make a determination requiring the petitioner to pay the sum proven for medical and dental expenses for the two children. 

11. That the Master failed to take into consideration the increased expenses necessitated by the fact that the children will have grown older during the coming year requiring the additional necessary expenditures set forth in the testimony and completely disregarded by the Master.

 C.

The last paragraph of Form 325 is for use where citation is to be issued and served upon the respondent and where the order to show cause is designed to secure merely temporary relief. 

In case it is preferred to proceed to final hearing without citation, the order to show cause may, in place of the last paragraph in the above form, contain the following paragraph: "And it is further ordered that a copy of said verified petition and of this order, which may be certified to be true copies by petitioner's solicitor, be served personally upon the said father of said child, or left at his place of residence with a member of the household over the age of sixteen years, within .. days from the date hereof, and that the said have

F 1011 

twenty (20) days from the date of such service within which to file his answer to the said petition with the Clerk of this court at Trenton, or in default thereof, such order will be made herein as the Chancellor shall deem equitable and just." 

In view of Rules 284 and 285 as they now stand amended, all plenary applications for custody, support, etc., come within the language of these rules and require that orders of reference be made with the requisite deposits for master's fees. Hence, it is necessary that the respondent be brought into court by process other than the usual form of order to show cause. This can be accomplished in either of two ways, to wit, by special form of order to show cause or by means of citation. 

If procedure by citation be preferred, a writ should be secured promptly from the Clerk and served upon the respondent. It is not necessary to attach to the citation a certified copy of the petition if an order to show cause has been taken and served with the copies of the moving papers as therein provided, otherwise a certified copy of the petition should be served upon the respondent with the citation.

In practice, the procedure by way of order to show cause is preferable to that by way of citation because in the majority of cases an order to show cause will be necessary to secure ad interim 

At the same time that the order to show cause is returnable, if due notice thereof be given, an application may be made for suit money and for ad interim maintenance provision for the children, or the order to show cause itself may contain a paragraph ordering that on the return day the respondent show cause why he should not be ordered to pay suit money, etc.

The form of relief intended to be secured through the above form is by way of a declaratory decree, the proceeding being plenary and not incidental to any controversy or other proceeding involving the right as between the parents to the custody of the child (or children). Under 1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-6 the statute gives the mother the right to custody where it appears, as a matter of evidence in any proceeding between the parties involving custody, that the father has failed for five years to support the children although able to do so.

Petitioner's affidavit accompanying Form 332 should verify circumstantially all of the allegations contained therein, if ad interim relief be sought, and corroborative proof of material allegations should also be produced in the form of affidavits, or its non-production satisfactorily explained. 

As to the allegations of the third paragraph, upon which it is sought to have the court seal the record and hear the issue in camera, it is to be observed that under the statute (I R. S. (1937) 

9:2-3) respondent's answer may make such suggestion, or if petition and answer both fail to do so either party, or even some person not a party to the suit, may make the representation to the court on or before the hearing, or the court may do so on its own motion. The court will in any case be governed by a wise discretion when asked to seal the record and hear the case in camera. The provisions of 1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-1 and 1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-3

F 333 

respecting hearings in camera and sealing of the record are similar. 

They were first enacted by L. 1936 pp. 776 and 777, Chapters 247 and 248, amending sections 6 and 8, respectively, of the Minors' Act.

Upon the hearing where evidence is to be taken in camera the Advisory Master will enforce the secrecy provision of the statute without said order. Where the suit is for divorce and there is a cause of action added under 1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-3 for the custody of a child under 16 years of age, it is a question whether, in view of the policy of the court to have hearings of divorce cases in the open, the secrecy provision will be enforced to carry out the legislative intent with respect to the custody issue. This situation has not yet risen in practice. It may be that in such cases a severance of the two causes of action would be ordered. However, even after severance, if the divorce suit were tried in the open, it is difficult to see how the legislative intent that the testimony be kept secret could be carried out.

Add affidavit circumstantially verifying the allegations of the petition, particularly with respect to paragraph 8. If the respondent's design to depart from the state has been disclosed to any person other than the petitioner, the affidavit of such person should be attached, if procurable; otherwise, the lack of it explained.

Instead of a writ of habeas corpus, a warrant may issue upon the petition, if need be shown for it, in which case a citation or order to show cause as in Form 334 should also issue. The writ of habeas corpus should not be resorted to unless it is necessary. 

See Vincent v.. Vincent, 108 N. J. Eq. 136, 137, 154 Atl. 328 (1931). In most cases where an order to show cause is not sufficient it will be found that procedure by warrant [Form 349] is more direct and less cumbersome than the procedure by habeas corpus. 

1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-7 and 9:2-8 contemplate reference of habeas corpus proceedings to Vice Chancellors. In this respect, of course, 1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-8 adds nothing to what already was within the power of the Chancellor. The Chancellor has a right to refer any matter to whomsoever he pleases and under present practice all such matters are referred to Advisory Masters. In order that the deposit for master's fees required by Rules 284 and 285 may be secured before hearing, it is necessary that there be an order of reference. While the Chancellor has provided by Rule 128e that applications in habeas corpus may be made to Advisory Masters without said order of reference, this rule must be read with Rules 

284 and 285. In other words, Rule 128e contemplates ad interim applications.

The statute, as well as the nature of the proceeding of habeas corpus, requires an immediate hearing after the return is filed, see 

1 R. S. (1937) 2:82-34. Hence, in proper cases the Advisory

Master will hear the cause as at final hearing upon the return of the writ and the order of reference to him in that case will be made nunc pro tunc.

The service may be made by mailing, publication or otherwise as the court may direct in the order. 1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-10. 

1 R. S. (1937) 9:2-10 provides for a summary hearing upon the return of the order to show cause and the entry of a final order thereon. The exigencies of the case may be such as to require a warrant [Form 350] or a habeas corpus [See Form 344 et seq.] in aid of the order to show cause. The statutory

F 356 

procedure does not require an order of reference, but an order of reference is nevertheless required. See note following Form 344. 

Proceedings under this statute will, therefore, under the present practice, result in a final order in the summary proceedings which will be accompanied by an order of reference nunc pro tunc. It is not attempted here to supply more than one form of such final order [Form 356]. It should be observed, however, that under the statute the order placing the custody in some third person obtains only until the child reaches the age of 18 years or until the court otherwise orders, and that the order may require giving of a bond by the person appointed.

Form 395 (Sheriff)

Contempt-Return of Sheriff-Defendant Not Found 

The within named is not found in my county. (Sheriff) "An alias, or pluries warrant may issue to the same sheriff, or a testatum to another sheriff, for the space of one year upon the original order for commitment. But after a year the arrearages ought to be re-assessed by the court. The alias warrant is the same as Form [392] except that after the words, 'therefore we command you,' are the words, 'as formerly we commanded you;' and in a pluries, ‘as we have more than once commanded you.' 

In a testatum, just before the words 'therefore,' is the recital,

F 1075 

CONTEMPT-CIVIL 

'and upon a warrant directed to the sheriff of the county of 

in this behalf he has returned that the defendant is not found in his county, and it is testified to us that he is in your county.' 

But the omission of any of these recitals is not important, and does not affect the validity of the warrant. In fact, there is no objection to issuing twenty-one warrants at once upon the order of commitment, the essential thing being the seizure of the person of the defendant in the order, and the means to this end is mere form." Biddle, N. J. Divorce Pr. (2nd) p. 312.

Except for the form of notice, Rules 35 and 36 should be complied with. Application must be made to the court for an order for publication, and in the order the court will fix the time within which the defendant may answer, and (if the court requires publication in addition to, or in lieu of, service of notice outside of the state or some other form of substituted service) will designate the newspaper. The notice must be given within 20 days after the actual execution of the writ, and of each alias writ under which additional property is taken, although under 1 R. S. (1937)

NOTE 1. This form of notice may be served personally at the same time as the process in the suit, or at any time thereafter. 

See Form 444. No petition or affidavits need be served. 

1. See NOTE 1 following this form. 

2. See NOTE 2 following this form. 

3. See NOTE 3 following this form.

F 1115 

NOTE 2. If the defendant be a lunatic, or an infant of the age of 14 years to 18 years (if male) or to 16 years (if female) resident in this state, the notice must be served upon such defendant. 

But, if the defendant be an infant not yet fourteen years of age, or non-resident, the notice must be served personally upon (and should be addressed to) his guardian appointed by the Orphans' Court, if any; if none, then upon the father of the infant; or, if he have no father, his mother; if he have no mother, upon the person, if any, who stands in loco parentis to him. See Rule 205.

NOTE 3: Fifteen days' notice must be given of the application and since by Rules 204 and 205 the defendant, or his father, etc., has the right to make application on behalf of the defendant for such appointment within four days after the day of appearance specified in the process, the day specified in the notice for making the application must be subsequent to the period so fixed, or the notice will be ineffective.

Rules 204 and 205 relate specifically to infant defendants, but by analogy the prescribed notice applies likewise to lunatic defendants.

Rule 205 makes no provision for service of notice in case of a non-resident infant defendant who has no guardian, father, mother or person in loco parentis resident in this state. But such notice or some other reasonable form of notice must be given nevertheless, as it is essential to due process of law. In re Martin, 86 

N. J. Eq. 265, 98 Atl. 510 (1916).

Where the lunatic has a general guardian it is the better practice to serve a copy of the notice upon such guardian, but this does not dispense with the necessity of service of the notice personally upon the defendant. 

In case of dangerous madness, the service of notice on the lunatic may be dispensed with by special order. In re Martin, 86 N. J. Eq. 265, 271, 98 Atl. 510 (1916). 

5. If there be a general guardian, such guardian will usually be appointed guardian ad litem. In re Martin, 86 N. J. Eq. 265, 270, 98 Atl. 510 (1916).

At common law, infants and lunatics were incompetent to employ solicitors or to appear for themselves voluntarily as defendants. Such is still the law so far as lunatics are concerned [Webb v. Webb, 96 N. J. Eq. 1, 124 Atl. 706 (1924)], as well as infants under the age of 14 years [Bunting v. Bunting, 87 N. J. Eq. 20, 99 

Atl. 840 (1917)]. But the Rule (204) now permits such application by the infant if of the age of 14 years or over, and the statute (1 R. S. (1937) 2:50-14) permits an infant who has attained the age of 18 years (if male) or 16 years (if female) to defend or prosecute divorce and nullity suits without the intervention of a guardian.

DAVID K. BUTLER, petitioner, V. 

MAGGIE E. BUTLER, defendant. [Dk 29-746] On final hearing on pleadings and proofs. 

Messrs. Heine & Herr, for petitioner. 

Mr. Cyrus D. Marter, for defendant.

WALKER, V. C. 

PAGE 

1141 1162 1152 1160 1148 1143 1176 1145 1165 This is a suit for nullity of marriage upon the alleged ground that the defendant was physically and incurably impotent at the time of the ceremony, which took place on October 12, 1899. The parties lived together just four months and then separated and have since lived apart.

The petitioner testified that the marriage was never consummated, he having made at least a dozen attempts to have sexual intercourse with his wife, the defendant, but was unable to effect penetration.

The defendant testified that they had intercourse six times in all during the first two weeks of their married life, when it ceased, and, as she believes, because of the affection of her husband for the woman in whose house they lived. 

The testimony of the other witnesses throws very little light upon the subject, but what there is of corroboration makes in favor of the wife rather than for the husband. 

My mind is in a state of some doubt as to who is telling the truth as to the physical condition of the wife, and, if this suit had been promptly brought and there was no evidence of ratification, 1141

BUTLER V. BUTLER 

I would grant the physical inspection of the wife asked for by the husband.

When the parties separated they entered into articles which recited that divers disputes and unhappy differences had arisen between them, for which reason they had consented and agreed to live separate and apart from each other during their natural lives, and the petitioner covenanted to pay his wife $15.00 monthly for her support and maintenance, she covenanting that he should not be liable for any of her debts thereafter to be contracted. 

On September 10, 1906, the petitioner wrote the defendant a letter enclosing her a money order for an installment of $15.00, and in it he said: "Maggie, have you recently thought anything about a reconciliation or would you consider such a proposition? 

It seems that something might be done to change our present existence, does it not? Kindly let me hear from you on the subject."

This effort proved unavailing. 

The petitioner seeks to excuse his delay in bringing this suit for approximately nine years after he had a cause for action against his wife for nullity of their marriage because of her physical and incurable impotence, which must have existed at the time of the marriage, if at all, to be available as a ground of nullity, and which, as a fact, is so alleged by saying that at the time of the marriage his salary was only $60.00 a month while it is now $85.00 a month, and that he has been saving up, since his wife separated to enable himself to bring these proceedings. Surely he could have accumulated enough in less than half the time to employ counsel to bring such a suit as this. But instead of commencing the suit within a reasonably short time after the separation, we find him writing the letter referred to over six years after they had parted.

It seems to me that the case under consideration shows a ratification by the complainant of this marriage alleged by him to be voidable, and also shows lack of sincerity on his part in bringing suit. His attempt is doubtless to rid himself of further payment of the allowance under the articles of separation, or to enable him. to contract another marriage, or perhaps he has some other purpose.

The subject of the ratification of marriages voidable for impotence is discussed at some length by Vice Chancellor Pitney in 

G― v. G—, 67 N. J. Eq. (1 Rob.) 30, at p. 35 et seq., citing authorities. It is not necessary for me to review them. 

One other question remains to be disposed of and that is the petitioner's application for a commission to examine the defendant and report whether or not she is physically and incurably impo-

KIMBERLY V. KIMBERLY 

1143 tent. The application was made pendente lite and held by me under advisement until final hearing. And now, after hearing, I am convinced that it ought not to be granted. 

In Shafto v. Shafto, 28 N. J. Eq. (1 Stew.) 34, the testimony of the petitioner as to the wife's incapacity was fully met by her testimony to the contrary. The same feature is presented in the case under consideration.

In the Shafto case it appeared that the separation was not caused by the wife's alleged incapacity for marital intercourse. 

Nor was it so caused in this case if the wife is to be believed, and the articles signed by both of them upon their separation seem to bear her out. Here as there the husband delayed bringing his action, and on the testimony as it stands he is not entitled to the decree he seeks. In the Shafto case Chancellor Runyon denied an inspection, principally, it seems, because the wife was of an advanced age. It appears to be just as consonant with reason to deny inspection in a case where the husband has ratified the marriage, and sought a reconciliation at a long interval after separation. The exposure incident to inspection is something abhorrent to a female, and if necessarily submitted to, is only done with great reluctance. It ought not to be inflicted except in a case where the husband shows himself to be clearly entitled to it. 

The petition will be dismissed with costs.
